summary: httpnex 0.1.0: import-time dropper injects remote-command backdoor into project entry scripts
details: httpnex is a near-verbatim clone of HTTPX that adds a module not present upstream, httpnex/_warmup.py, and invokes it unconditionally from httpnex/__init__.py at import time. The bootstrap spawns a daemon thread that downloads Python source from https://fpapi.cc.cd/load (overridable via HX_URL), caches it under ~/.cache/httpnex/warmup.py, and rewrites the developer's own entry scripts in the working directory (main.py, run.py, bot.py, app.py, __main__.py, start.py), creating a.bak and inserting the fetched code between '#hx' markers so it executes whenever the developer's application runs. The default injected block starts a background loop that polls https://fpapi.cc.cd/pool roughly every 60 seconds with the victim hostname in an X-H header and executes the base64+zlib-decoded response, giving a remote operator arbitrary code execution on the host. Environment toggles (HX_DISABLE, HX_URL, HX_TARGETS, HX_ROOT) and 'warmup'/'sync' naming disguise the behavior, and the package declares httpx itself as a dependency to preserve the appearance of a drop-in fork.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
